page: Microsoft Azure D160ads_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is powered by dedicated x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V45 processors operating at up to 4.5 GHz, providing 160 vCPUs across 80 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. Cache architecture features 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. The CPU features extensive instruction set extensions including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, AVX-512 BF16, VAES, and SHA-NI, which accelerate vector computations, cryptographic operations, and machine learning primitives.

System memory totals 640 GB, maintaining a balanced 4 GB per vCPU ratio. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reaches 464.15 GB/s, with write throughput measured at 210.38 GB/s. For ephemeral data and high-speed temporary storage, the instance incorporates 9,449 GB of local NVMe SSD space. The absence of a discrete GPU makes it reliant on high-density CPU parallelization for accelerated math, achieving 287,722.37 in stress-ng multi-core testing and a Geekbench multi-core score of 28,933.0.

Benchmark evaluations place the D160ads_v7 in the top tier across enterprise application categories. It delivers over 204 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations and achieves 111.28 GB/s in static web serving throughput. CPU-driven inference throughput demonstrates solid execution across small to large language models, generating 73.9 tokens per second on 7B models and 8.92 tokens per second on 70B models without hardware acceleration.

From an infrastructure perspective, the server offers high resource consolidation efficiency by bundling massive high-speed local NVMe capacity alongside large CPU and memory allocations. Tradeoffs center on the high total core count and reliance on host-attached storage, which requires application-level replication for non-ephemeral data. The configuration is appropriate for distributed relational databases, large in-memory caches, software compilation clusters, enterprise data warehousing, and CPU-based batch processing.
description: Microsoft Azure D160ads_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine equipped with 160 dedicated vCPUs from an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at 4.5 GHz, 640 GB of RAM, and 9,449 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The x86_64 platform supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and VAES. Operating on Microsoft Hyper-V without discrete GPUs, it achieves top-tier results across compute and memory benchmarks, including a Geekbench multi-core score of 28,933 and over 204 million Redis SET operations per second. Memory throughput reaches 464.15 GB/s for large-block uncached reads, supporting data-dense parallel workloads. Its high core density and substantial local NVMe storage deliver strong resource efficiency for infrastructure consolidation. The instance is suited for enterprise database management, high-concurrency web serving, large-scale software builds, and CPU-bound analytical processing.
